summary:
LUNA: Mission Survival is an interactive 3D educational game designed for children aged 7–12. It takes players on an exciting journey to explore and manage a lunar colony while learning about the challenges astronauts face when living on the Moon.

Players explore a 3D lunar environment, interact with colony facilities, and complete survival missions involving power generation, water collection, radiation protection, food production, habitat maintenance, and communication.

Through hands-on mini-games and a friendly AI companion named ORBIT, children learn how essential resources work together to keep astronauts safe. The project incorporates NASA space-weather data from the DONKI database to introduce real solar energetic particle events through simulated gameplay scenarios.

LUNA aims to make space science more engaging and accessible by transforming complex space exploration concepts into an interactive learning adventure.
details:
Project Overview

LUNA: Mission Survival is a browser-based 3D lunar colony survival game developed to make space exploration understandable and exciting for children aged 7–12.

How It Works

Players enter a simulated lunar colony and explore different facilities, including the main habitat, greenhouse, solar array, research laboratory and communication antenna.

The game is structured around a seven-day mission. Each day introduces a practical survival challenge through interactive gameplay and mini-games. Players perform activities such as repairing solar panels, collecting water, protecting astronauts during solar events, growing food and restoring communication systems.

A friendly robot companion, ORBIT, guides players with short instructions and hints. Mission progress and colony resources respond to player actions, helping children understand how astronauts depend on essential systems to survive.

NASA Data Integration

The project uses NASA's DONKI Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) event records to introduce real space-weather events into the solar-storm mission. The game translates scientific event information into simplified scenarios. Astronaut health effects and gameplay consequences are simulations, not actual radiation measurements.

Technology Used

  • Three.js for the interactive 3D environment.
  • JavaScript for gameplay and simulation logic.
  • HTML and CSS for the user interface.
  • Vite for development and building.
  • NASA DONKI for space-weather data.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNA introduces children to lunar exploration, resource management, solar activity and astronaut safety through hands-on experiences rather than lengthy explanations or traditional quizzes.

Its goal is to encourage curiosity about space science, develop problem-solving skills and help young learners understand the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence beyond Earth.

Creativity

The project combines a 3D lunar environment, interactive facilities, mission-based mini-games, resource management and a friendly robot companion to create an engaging space survival experience.
